name: N7SIX ApeX Edition v7.6.10
body:
{"value" => "N7SIX ApeX Edition v7.6.10 (UV-K5/K5(8)/K6 v1)

**Release date:** September 21, 2026
**Build target:** UV-K5 / UV-K5(8) / UV-K6 (Version 1)
**Commit:** 504e58f

## Getting Started
- Firmware: **n7six.ApeX-k5.v7.6.10.packed.bin** (attached to this release)
- Flasher: UVTools - https://n7six.github.io/UVTools/
- To compile: `./compile-with-docker.sh ApeX` (Docker) or `win_make.bat` (Windows)

## Today's Updates Included

### UI/UX Enhancements
- **Adopted UI/UX from UV-K1 latest Fusion (Armel, F4HWN)**: The interface now incorporates the latest UI/UX design patterns from the UV-K1's Fusion firmware by Armel (F4HWN), providing a more intuitive and polished user experience with improved navigation and visual consistency.

### Battery System
- **2-point Battery Calibration**: Implemented a 2-point battery calibration system that allows for more accurate battery voltage-to-percentage and remaining capacity estimation across the full discharge curve. This replaces the previous single-point estimation with a more precise curve-fitting approach.

### Spectrum Analyzer
- **Waterfall Disabled (Temporary)**: The waterfall implementation has been temporarily disabled to reduce FLASH usage. This feature will be re-enabled once ample FLASH space is reclaimed. The spectrum analyzer itself remains fully functional - only the temporal waterfall layer is off.

### System Information (SysInf)
- **Build ID (git commit) now shown on the BUILD page**: The `SysInf` -> `BUILD` page previously always displayed `N/A`. The build now embeds the short git commit hash at compile time, so you can verify exactly which revision is running on the radio (this release shows `504e58f`).

## Memory Usage
```
Memory Region      Used Size  Region Size   % Used
FLASH                61280        61440     99.74%
RAM                   3372         8192     41.16%
```

## How to Flash
1. Download **n7six.ApeX-k5.v7.6.10.packed.bin** from the Assets section below.
2. Flash it with UVTools (https://n7six.github.io/UVTools/) or k5prog.
3. After boot, open `SysInf` and check the BUILD page: it shows the build date, time and the embedded commit ID (`504e58f`).

## Credits
Many thanks to Egzumer, OneOfEleven, DualTachyon, Mikhail Andrej, Manuel @wagner, @lohtse, Shar @Matoz, @davide, @Ismo OH2FTG, OneOfEleven @d1ced95, and others.
